 Tropical moisture and favorable atmospheric conditions are fueling a flood risk this week across the Southwest. Severe storms are also possible, especially across Arizona. 
 Happening now
 Severe storms and bands of heavy rainfall are hitting parts of the Four Corners region. 
 Heavy rain and flooding have hit southern Utah particularly hard this Thursday, including the town of Hurricane where evacuation orders have been issued.

 Flood threat
 Moisture will continue to pump into the Southwest into Friday, only enhancing the flood threat on already saturated soils. 
 This threat will shift east and likely decrease some during the day on Friday toward the Southern Rockies and Southern High Plains

 Some of the biggest concerns will be the possibility of mudslides over recent burn scar areas as well as slot canyons and arroyos. 
 If you have plans to visit any of the national parks in the West this week, make sure you check the forecast daily and pay attention to any warnings or advisories issued.
 Severe threat 
 A few strong thunderstorms could also produce hail, a strong wind gust or two and an isolated tornado in New Mexico on Friday. 
 How much rain and snow is expected?
 Up to 5 inches of rain is possible in New Mexico and southern Colorado through the end of the week, which is more than enough for flash flooding in this region. Up to 3 inches are possible from the Texas Panhandle to southeastern South Dakota by the end of the weekend. 
 And yes, we could even squeeze some snow out of this system for some of the higher elevations. 
 Parts of the Colorado Rockies could see the first significant snow of the season. This could be a nice base for some of the ski resorts that were robbed of snow last winter. 
 While widespread snowfall totals will stay under 6 inches, we could see isolated peaks pick up one to two feet of snow. 
 Make sure you check back often, as the forecast could change. And don’t be caught off-guard if you are traveling through some of the higher elevations, as the rain could change to snow quickly.
 Recap
 Downtown Flagstaff reported hail the size of golfballs, or 1.75 inches in diameter, on Wednesday. There was also a gust to 72 mph at the Flagstaff Airport. 
 The first tornado watch was issued for northern Arizona in more than 16 years on Wednesday. A second watch was issued for eastern Arizona and western New Mexico on Thursday.
